programme.title: The UnXplained with William Shatner
programme.desc: S3 E16 — Superhuman FeatsWhether surviving freezing temperatures, diving unfathomable depths in one breath or lifting weighty objects, there have been numerous instances of extraordinary superhuman feats. The actor examines whether pulling them off is a matter of training, willpower, genetics or something more mysterious.

programme.title: The UnXplained with William Shatner
programme.desc: S5 E3 — The LostPeople go missing every day, but throughout history there have been strange and eerie disappearances. They range from iconic figures such as aviation Amelia Earhart to entire groups. These strange disappearances, lacking definitive explanations, have fuelled numerous theories over time, captivating global attention.

programme.title: Strange Evidence
programme.desc: S2 E1 — Freak of the DeepAn instance in which a mother and child fled in terror as the entire roof of a building mysteriously ripped off and flew towards them. Plus, how scientists were left baffled as a truck carrying nothing but paint inexplicably exploded on a busy motorway and how deep-sea explorers discovered a monster thousands of feet deep in the ocean.

programme.title: Strange Evidence
programme.desc: S2 E2 — America's Loch Ness MonsterA Vermont woman films a Loch Ness Monster-esque creature in America's Lake Champlain. Some fear it could be Champ, a legendary plesiosaur-like creature that has been witnessed in the spot over 100 years. Deep in Russia, an enormous explosion is captured on a car's dash cam.

programme.title: The Proof Is Out There
programme.desc: S3 E17 — UFO Lead, Bigfoot Films, and the Lost City in the Gulf of MexicoThe notion that a video leak from the Department of Homeland Security offers more evidence that UFOs really exist. Plus, a consideration of whether one of the world's most respected Bigfoot researchers really did manage to capture footage that proves Sasquatch is no myth.

programme.title: The Proof Is Out There
programme.desc: S3 E19 — Mutant Mermaid, UFOs vs Nukes and Seamonster Chases a BoatScientists study claims of a dead mermaid discovered and preserved in Japan. Plus a glowing-eyed sea creature captured on video chasing a motorboat and the connection between a man who lived alone in the jungle for over a quarter of a century and a fabled lost city in the Amazon.

programme.title: The Proof Is Out There
programme.desc: S3 E20 — Alien Sabotage, Ghost Child and Hungry Hungry SasquatchAn examination of several seemingly impossible things 'caught on film'. A species of carnivorous marsupials, thought to be long extinct, are suspected of being caught on camera. Plus, the notion that a visitor at a historic cemetery in Savannah captured a 'ghost child.

programme.title: What on Earth?
programme.desc: S4 E1 — Season 4Documentary exploring anomalies appearing on satellite images to try to get a better understanding of unexplained phenomena. An image of a wrecked aeroplane triggers a hunt that leads to a Colombian drug lord, a series of mounds in Romania provide possible evidence of a vampire burial site, while a mysterious ancient city is spotted on a coral reef.

programme.title: What on Earth?
programme.desc: S4 E2 — Season 4Documentary exploring anomalies appearing on satellite images. After 70 years, images help identify the hiding place of the multi-billion dollar Nazi Gold Train, while a blood-red river in Siberia points to pollution on a catastrophic scale. Plus, satellite evidence indicates the Vikings may have travelled further into North America than anyone previously imagined.

programme.title: What on Earth?
programme.desc: S4 E3 — Season 4A structure shaped like a giant shark provides likely evidence of a Bahamian lost civilisation. Plus, the satellite images of hundreds of thousands of strange oval scars on the North American landscape leaving experts baffled and analysis of an image of a massive hurricane that shows it has thousands of animals trapped in its eye.

programme.title: Ghost Ships
programme.desc: S1 E3 — Halifax ExplosionAn event in December 1917, when the SS Mont Blanc and the SS Imo accidentally crashed into each other in Halifax Harbour. The resulting explosion destroyed over 10,000 buildings and left approximately 25,000 people without shelter. Now, professional salvage diver Tony Sampson and his team to brave chilled waters in search of wreckage.

programme.title: Ghost Ships
programme.desc: S1 E4 — SS Clare LilleyFor decades, residents of Portuguese Cove, Nova Scotia, have reported unexploded ordnance washing up on their shores. The local government has tried to clean it up, but the munitions keep coming. Professional salvage diver Tony Sampson and his team dive in search of SS Clare Lilley to get to the bottom of this potentially explosive wreck.

programme.title: Hazardous History with Henry Winkler
programme.desc: S1 E7 — Precarious ProductsThe presenter explores the everyday items that many people use without realising how dangerous they can be. From cleaning supplies to personal care products, he reveals the hidden dangers that lurk in people's homes.

programme.title: Hitler's Engineers
programme.desc: S1 E1 — Albert SpeerThe sinister role that planners, designers, architects and builders played in shaping the Second World War, thus helping Adolf Hitler retain power. In his role as Adolf Hitler's favourite architect, Albert Speer was a central figure in the Fuhrer's inner circle and helped cement his position.

programme.title: U-Boat Wargamers
programme.desc: S1 E1 — The MastermindThe remarkable story of retired war gamer Gilbert Roberts, officer Jean Laidlaw and the Women's Royal Navy Service (WRNS) - aka the 'Wrens' - as they use revolutionary war gaming tactics to defeat Admiral Karl Dönitz and his Wolf Pack fleets of U-boats in the Battle of the Atlantic during the Second World War. The Second World War breaks out and a force of U-boats try to starve Britain into submission. Meanwhile, Vera Laughton Mathews recruits talented women into the WRNS. Narrated by Derek Jacobi.

programme.title: Weird Britain
programme.desc: S2 E11 — SomersetAndy McGrath embarks on an inspiring journey back to Somerset, where he conducts a ghost hunt in the infamous Shepton Mallet Prison, and visits the magnificent SS Great Britain in Bristol.

programme.title: Weird Britain
programme.desc: S2 E12 — Weird EventsIn search of adventure, Andy McGrath decides to participate in some of Britain's weirdest events. He watches fearless competitors from around the world chase a wheel of cheese down a 180-metre hill in Gloucestershire.

programme.title: The Proof Is Out There
programme.desc: S4 E2 — UFO Over the Andes, the Ohio Grassman and Ancient Horn MysteryThe legendary Ohio Grassman is apparently captured in footage of a tall, dark-coloured, hairy creature walking through woods. Plus, a look at the Chilean family photograph of a 'real UFO' flying above the Andes Mountains and the notion that a 5,000-year-old horn discovered on a beach in England belongs to a prehistoric creature that still lives.

programme.title: UFOs: The Lost Evidence

programme.title: Walking Through History
programme.desc: S2 E2 — Romans in the LakesIt was 30 years after the Romans invaded Britain that they were ready to take on the challenge of conquering the Lake District. With the toughest landscape they had encountered in the nation, peopled by a rebellious tribe, it was no small task, but within a few years, the whole of Lakeland was under their control. Tony Robinson tackles the journey by himself, walking 50 miles from Penrith to Ambleside and on to the Irish Sea at Ravenglass, discovering that the Romans encountered beauty and danger in equal measure.

programme.title: Walking Through History
programme.desc: S2 E3 — Smugglers' CornwallTony Robinson takes a four-day trek along the coastline between Plymouth in Devon and Falmouth, learning about the thriving smuggling trade in Cornwall during the late 18th century. The area's tiny secretive harbours, beaches and secluded coves were ideal for illicit imports such as tobacco and brandy, and the business was so huge it threatened the national economy. Along his route, visiting such beauty spots as Lantic Bay and Polperro, he encounters all sorts of reminders of the trade and meets descendants of those involved.

Their first stop is Wapping Wharf, a series of shipping containers housing everything from a butcher to a cheese-monger. After a bit of shopping, James pitches up his mobile kitchen overlooking the iconic Clifton Suspension Bridge to make a tagine of lamb chops.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S32 E5 — Standout SeafoodA seafood spot in Vancouver combines sustainability with killer cooking, including bouillabaisse and salmon fish and chips. A fresh-catch institution in Kauai puts out prime-time poke. A raw bar in Chico cooks up Asian flavours.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S32 E7 — Crazy Chicken and Twisted BurgersGuy Fieri's digging into crazy twists on chicken and burgers; in Wilmington, Del., there's a bourbon bar that's piling pork onto a patty and doctoring up chicken skins.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S32 E8 — International InfusionGrub infused with international flavours; a spot in Wilmington, Del., puts Thai into sausage and Cuban into sandwiches; in Kauai, there's a Tiki joint cooking up Hawaiian flair; a Lebanese place in San Diego is serving authentic specialities.

programme.title: Diners, Drive-Ins and Dives
programme.desc: S18 E6 — Sammies and StewIn Santa Fe, New Mexico, ma hi and Caribbean goat stew, in Albuquerque, New Mexico, turkey avocado with green apple chilli chutney and a Duke City Reuben.

programme.title: River Cottage: Every Day
programme.desc: S15 E1 — MeatHugh Fearnley-Whittingstall sets out his belief that the way to be able to make organic free-range meat fit your budget, is to eat and enjoy cheap cuts rather than cheap meat. He's off to a butcher for ox liver. Devilled in a hot and spicy sauce it proves to be a real winner. Hugh takes his passion for cheap, cheerful and hearty stews to a local five-aside team, where he suffers footballing failure.

programme.title: The Hairy Bikers' Comfort Food
programme.desc: S1 E4 — Come on OverThe Bikers cook the perfect dishes to share with the people we love. These are indulgent treats for when family and friends come on over. A baked cheesecake, a crowd pleasing terrine and the ultimate beef sandwich.

programme.title: Delicious Miss Brown
programme.desc: S1 E3 — Picnic in the ParkKardea picnics in the park with friends and provides them with some tasty bites. She makes rotisserie chicken sandwiches with homemade bacon jam plus more.

programme.title: Delicious Miss Brown
programme.desc: S1 E6 — Family ReunionKardea's family are all back together and she is hosting. On the menu is her family favourite no-fuss baby back ribs, a four-bean salad and a delicious potato salad.

programme.title: Jamie's 15 Minute Meals
programme.desc: S1 E39 — Sausage Gnocchi and Mexican ChickenWith sausage gnocchi, warm kale and bean salad, and Mexican chicken, wicked mole sauce, veg and rice.

programme.title: Jamie's 15 Minute Meals
programme.desc: S1 E40 — Asian Sea Bass and Chorizo CarbonaraIn the last of the series, Jamie Oliver cooks Asian sea bass, sticky rice and dressed greens, plus chorizo carbonara and Catalan market salad.

programme.title: Be My Guest With Ina Garten
programme.desc: S4 E6 — David RemnickIt's a dream come true for Ina Garten when she invites Pulitzer Prize-winning author and journalist David Remnick to the barn. Ina welcomes him with overnight Belgian waffles and hosts a Parmesan chicken cooking class before dinner in the garden.

programme.title: Be My Guest With Ina Garten
programme.desc: S5 E5 — Ann PatchettAward-winning novelist Ann Patchett joins Ina Garten for a fun-filled day at the barn. Ina welcomes her with a rustic cherry clafouti, and for lunch, they share Charlie Bird's farro salad with Ina's jammy eggs and Ann's favourite roasted cauliflower.

programme.title: The Great British Bake Off
programme.desc: S13 E6 — Halloween WeekHalloween has come early as the remaining bakers tackle three terrifying challenges. There's a seasonal Signature in the form of an apple cake, followed by a moreish Technical and, in the Showstopper, they create a Halloween piñata.

programme.title: Rachel Allen: Bake!
programme.desc: Christmas Bake IHere, Rachel makes a tasty Christmas cake and is joined by Gennaro Contaldo to bake zuccotto di panettone.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Brazil v HaitiBrazil v Haiti (Kick-off 1.30am). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group C match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. Brazil were second best for most of their opener against Morocco, but came away with a 1-1 draw, while Haiti performed admirably in a 1-0 defeat to Scotland. Brazil have registered large victories in the two previous encounters between these nations, claiming a 6-0 win in an international friendly in 2004, and more recently a 7-1 triumph in the group stage of the 2016 Copa America, which also took place in the United States, and saw then-Liverpool attacking midfielder Philippe Coutinho score a hat-trick. Despite a relatively poor record in qualifying the Seleção will have high hopes of performing well under the stewardship of former Real Madrid, Chelsea and AC Milan manager Carlo Ancelotti, who was appointed in May last year on a one-year contract, which has since been extended for another four years, and anything other than a victory in this match will be considered a catastrophe. With analysis from Karen Carney and Emma Hayes, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Türkiye v ParaguayTürkiye v Paraguay (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group D match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in Santa Clara, USA. Both sides need something from this fixture, with Türkiye abject in their 2-0 defeat to Australia, and Paraguay blown away by the USA in their opening contests. There has only been one previous meeting between these nations, a 0-0 draw in a 1995 friendly, but Paraguay will hope to emulate their results against European opposition in the group stage at their last World Cup appearance in South Africa in 2010, when they drew 1-1 against Italy and defeated Slovakia 2-0 on their way to finishing top of Group F. They subsequently overcame Japan in the last-16 via a penalty shootout, but then fell foul of a European nation in the quarter-finals, when they lost 1-0 to eventual champions Spain. With analysis from Juan Mata and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: James Martin's Great British Adventure
programme.desc: S1 E2 — LossiemouthJames Martin and his travelling companion Nick Nairn continue their Scottish adventure in Lossiemouth, home to the first RAF squadron and a fleet of typhoon fighter jets. James fulfils a childhood dream and Nick takes part in a fitness test.

programme.title: Love Your Garden
programme.desc: S12 E2 — ColourAlan Titchmarsh, David Domoney and Danny Clarke transform a small Leicester garden into a Caribbean-inspired paradise, showcasing how colour can reinvigorate outdoor spaces of any shape or size. Meanwhile in a separate garden, Frances Tophill reveals how to use light colour landscaping and shade loving flowers to bring vibrancy to dark and dingy corners.

programme.title: Ainsley's Fantastic Flavours
programme.desc: S3 E9 — Sweet DelightsAinsley Harriott makes a selection of dishes with a sweet twist, including Korean-inspired pork skewers and an American favourite with spicy and sweet buffalo sauce. Paralympic swimmer Ellie Simmonds pops in to show how to make her family recipe for chocolate cheesecake, and Ainsley samples another Maltese classic.

programme.title: Dermot's Taste of Ireland
programme.desc: S2 E8 — Donegal TownDermot reaches Donegal Town, discovering a place where Irish tradition and global flavours sit side by side. His day begins at family-run Hannah Hats, where he's fitted in iconic Donegal tweed and learns why this rugged corner of Ireland became famous for its flecked fabric. He visits Chandpur, widely regarded as Ireland's best curry house, where he and Bangladeshi-born chef Rana cook railway curry using outstanding local lamb and potatoes. For pudding, Dermot bakes a classic Irish apple pie with chef Brian McDermott, who explain how the rain improves local produce.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026
programme.desc: S5 E19 — Germany v Ivory CoastGermany v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. In four meetings against teams from Europe, they have a record of one win, one draw and two losses, with the sole win coming against Serbia and Montenegro at the 2006 tournament in Germany. While Die Mannschaft have a proud World Cup record overall they have failed to deliver since lifting the trophy in 2014, not even progressing beyond the group stage in both 2018 and 2022 after finishing fourth and third in the group standings respectively. Both sides got their campaigns underway with victories on the first gameday, as Germany thrashed Curacao 7-1 and Ivory Coast nicked a late 1-0 win against Ecuador.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026

There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. Both sides got their campaigns underway with victories on the first gameday, as Germany thrashed Curacao 7-1 and Ivory Coast nicked a late 1-0 win against Ecuador.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Brazil v HaitiBrazil v Haiti (Kick-off 1.30am). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group C match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. Brazil were second best for most of their opener against Morocco, but came away with a 1-1 draw, while Haiti performed admirably in a 1-0 defeat to Scotland. Brazil have registered large victories in the two previous encounters between these nations, claiming a 6-0 win in an international friendly in 2004, and more recently a 7-1 triumph in the group stage of the 2016 Copa America, which also took place in the United States, and saw then-Liverpool attacking midfielder Philippe Coutinho score a hat-trick. Despite a relatively poor record in qualifying the Seleção will have high hopes of performing well under the stewardship of former Real Madrid, Chelsea and AC Milan manager Carlo Ancelotti, who was appointed in May last year on a one-year contract, which has since been extended for another four years, and anything other than a victory in this match will be considered a catastrophe. With analysis from Karen Carney and Emma Hayes, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Türkiye v ParaguayTürkiye v Paraguay (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group D match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in Santa Clara, USA. Both sides need something from this fixture, with Türkiye abject in their 2-0 defeat to Australia, and Paraguay blown away by the USA in their opening contests. There has only been one previous meeting between these nations, a 0-0 draw in a 1995 friendly, but Paraguay will hope to emulate their results against European opposition in the group stage at their last World Cup appearance in South Africa in 2010, when they drew 1-1 against Italy and defeated Slovakia 2-0 on their way to finishing top of Group F. They subsequently overcame Japan in the last-16 via a penalty shootout, but then fell foul of a European nation in the quarter-finals, when they lost 1-0 to eventual champions Spain. With analysis from Juan Mata and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026
programme.desc: S5 E19 — Germany v Ivory CoastGermany v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. In four meetings against teams from Europe, they have a record of one win, one draw and two losses, with the sole win coming against Serbia and Montenegro at the 2006 tournament in Germany. While Die Mannschaft have a proud World Cup record overall they have failed to deliver since lifting the trophy in 2014, not even progressing beyond the group stage in both 2018 and 2022 after finishing fourth and third in the group standings respectively. Both sides got their campaigns underway with victories on the first gameday, as Germany thrashed Curacao 7-1 and Ivory Coast nicked a late 1-0 win against Ecuador.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026
programme.desc: S5 E19 — Germany v Ivory CoastGermany v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. In four meetings against teams from Europe, they have a record of one win, one draw and two losses, with the sole win coming against Serbia and Montenegro at the 2006 tournament in Germany. While Die Mannschaft have a proud World Cup record overall they have failed to deliver since lifting the trophy in 2014, not even progressing beyond the group stage in both 2018 and 2022 after finishing fourth and third in the group standings respectively. Both sides got their campaigns underway with victories on the first gameday, as Germany thrashed Curacao 7-1 and Ivory Coast nicked a late 1-0 win against Ecuador.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Brazil v HaitiBrazil v Haiti (Kick-off 1.30am). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group C match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. Brazil were second best for most of their opener against Morocco, but came away with a 1-1 draw, while Haiti performed admirably in a 1-0 defeat to Scotland. Brazil have registered large victories in the two previous encounters between these nations, claiming a 6-0 win in an international friendly in 2004, and more recently a 7-1 triumph in the group stage of the 2016 Copa America, which also took place in the United States, and saw then-Liverpool attacking midfielder Philippe Coutinho score a hat-trick. Despite a relatively poor record in qualifying the Seleção will have high hopes of performing well under the stewardship of former Real Madrid, Chelsea and AC Milan manager Carlo Ancelotti, who was appointed in May last year on a one-year contract, which has since been extended for another four years, and anything other than a victory in this match will be considered a catastrophe. With analysis from Karen Carney and Emma Hayes, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Türkiye v ParaguayTürkiye v Paraguay (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group D match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in Santa Clara, USA. Both sides need something from this fixture, with Türkiye abject in their 2-0 defeat to Australia, and Paraguay blown away by the USA in their opening contests. There has only been one previous meeting between these nations, a 0-0 draw in a 1995 friendly, but Paraguay will hope to emulate their results against European opposition in the group stage at their last World Cup appearance in South Africa in 2010, when they drew 1-1 against Italy and defeated Slovakia 2-0 on their way to finishing top of Group F. They subsequently overcame Japan in the last-16 via a penalty shootout, but then fell foul of a European nation in the quarter-finals, when they lost 1-0 to eventual champions Spain. With analysis from Juan Mata and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026
programme.desc: S5 E19 — Germany v Ivory CoastGermany v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. In four meetings against teams from Europe, they have a record of one win, one draw and two losses, with the sole win coming against Serbia and Montenegro at the 2006 tournament in Germany. While Die Mannschaft have a proud World Cup record overall they have failed to deliver since lifting the trophy in 2014, not even progressing beyond the group stage in both 2018 and 2022 after finishing fourth and third in the group standings respectively. Both sides got their campaigns underway with victories on the first gameday, as Germany thrashed Curacao 7-1 and Ivory Coast nicked a late 1-0 win against Ecuador.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Belgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Both these sides drew their opening group matches with Belgium drawing 1-1 against Egypt, while Iran twice came from behind to draw 2-2 with New Zealand. programme.desc: New Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Brazil v HaitiBrazil v Haiti (Kick-off 1.30am). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group C match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. Brazil were second best for most of their opener against Morocco, but came away with a 1-1 draw, while Haiti performed admirably in a 1-0 defeat to Scotland. Brazil have registered large victories in the two previous encounters between these nations, claiming a 6-0 win in an international friendly in 2004, and more recently a 7-1 triumph in the group stage of the 2016 Copa America, which also took place in the United States, and saw then-Liverpool attacking midfielder Philippe Coutinho score a hat-trick. Despite a relatively poor record in qualifying the Seleção will have high hopes of performing well under the stewardship of former Real Madrid, Chelsea and AC Milan manager Carlo Ancelotti, who was appointed in May last year on a one-year contract, which has since been extended for another four years, and anything other than a victory in this match will be considered a catastrophe. programme.desc: Türkiye v ParaguayTürkiye v Paraguay (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group D match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in Santa Clara, USA. Both sides need something from this fixture, with Türkiye abject in their 2-0 defeat to Australia, and Paraguay blown away by the USA in their opening contests. There has only been one previous meeting between these nations, a 0-0 draw in a 1995 friendly, but Paraguay will hope to emulate their results against European opposition in the group stage at their last World Cup appearance in South Africa in 2010, when they drew 1-1 against Italy and defeated Slovakia 2-0 on their way to finishing top of Group F. They subsequently overcame Japan in the last-16 via a penalty shootout, but then fell foul of a European nation in the quarter-finals, when they lost 1-0 to eventual champions Spain. With analysis from Juan Mata and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Brazil v HaitiBrazil v Haiti (Kick-off 1.30am). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group C match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. Brazil were second best for most of their opener against Morocco, but came away with a 1-1 draw, while Haiti performed admirably in a 1-0 defeat to Scotland. Brazil have registered large victories in the two previous encounters between these nations, claiming a 6-0 win in an international friendly in 2004, and more recently a 7-1 triumph in the group stage of the 2016 Copa America, which also took place in the United States, and saw then-Liverpool attacking midfielder Philippe Coutinho score a hat-trick. Despite a relatively poor record in qualifying the Seleção will have high hopes of performing well under the stewardship of former Real Madrid, Chelsea and AC Milan manager Carlo Ancelotti, who was appointed in May last year on a one-year contract, which has since been extended for another four years, and anything other than a victory in this match will be considered a catastrophe. With analysis from Karen Carney and Emma Hayes, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Türkiye v ParaguayTürkiye v Paraguay (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group D match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in Santa Clara, USA. Both sides need something from this fixture, with Türkiye abject in their 2-0 defeat to Australia, and Paraguay blown away by the USA in their opening contests. There has only been one previous meeting between these nations, a 0-0 draw in a 1995 friendly, but Paraguay will hope to emulate their results against European opposition in the group stage at their last World Cup appearance in South Africa in 2010, when they drew 1-1 against Italy and defeated Slovakia 2-0 on their way to finishing top of Group F. They subsequently overcame Japan in the last-16 via a penalty shootout, but then fell foul of a European nation in the quarter-finals, when they lost 1-0 to eventual champions Spain. With analysis from Juan Mata and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026
programme.desc: S5 E19 — Germany v Ivory CoastGermany v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. In four meetings against teams from Europe, they have a record of one win, one draw and two losses, with the sole win coming against Serbia and Montenegro at the 2006 tournament in Germany. While Die Mannschaft have a proud World Cup record overall they have failed to deliver since lifting the trophy in 2014, not even progressing beyond the group stage in both 2018 and 2022 after finishing fourth and third in the group standings respectively. Both sides got their campaigns underway with victories on the first gameday, as Germany thrashed Curacao 7-1 and Ivory Coast nicked a late 1-0 win against Ecuador.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E20 — Belgium v IranBelgium v Iran (Kick-off 8.00pm). Group G continues at Los Angeles Stadium in Inglewood, USA, where the sides face each other for the first time in their history. Some of the Iranian players may be familiar to fans of England and Wales, having been drawn in the same group four years ago in Qatar, with mixed results. A 6-2 drubbing at the hands of England was followed by a 2-0 win against Wales, with both goals coming deep into injury time. They'll start as underdogs here against Belgium, whose manager Rudi Garcia is leading them for the first time in a major finals, having taken over the reins at the start of last year. Despite a star-studded squad, Belgium have flattered to deceive and were ignominiously dumped out of the tournament four years ago, scoring just one goal, and that in an unconvincing win against Canada. Mark Pougatch presents, with analysis from Emma Hayes, Patrick Vieira and Roy Keane, and commentary by Joe Speight and Lucy Ward.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: S5 E21 — New Zealand v EgyptNew Zealand v Egypt (Kick-off 2.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the second Group G match for both sides, which takes place at BC Place Vancouver in Canada. New Zealand had yet to win a fixture at a World Cup finals in their previous attempts in 1982 and 2010 but, in part due to the huge number of teams now taking part, they were afforded one of the most comfortable paths to qualification of all nations. They defeated Tahiti, Samoa and Vanuatu in the group stage of the Oceania section, and followed that with knockout victories against Fiji and New Caledonia, with Nottingham Forest striker Chris Wood finishing that campaign as the leading scorer. This fixture should prove a much greater test of their credentials, in the first meeting between the sides since March 2024, when New Zealand finished fourth of four nations in the FIFA Series: Egypt. A Mostafa Mohamed Ahmed Abdallah penalty was the difference between the two on that occasion, and victory for either here would be a huge step towards reaching the knockout stage. New Zealand led twice in their opening group game on Monday before drawing 2-2 with Iran, while Egypt had to settle for a 1-1 draw against Belgium. With analysis from Ange Postecoglou and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.title: FIFA WC2026
programme.desc: S5 E19 — Germany v Ivory CoastGermany v Ivory Coast (Kick-off 9.00pm). Coverage of the Group E match at Toronto Stadium in Canada. There has only been one previous encounter between these nations, a 2009 friendly match that ended in a 2-2 draw in Gelsenkirchen, and Les Éléphants will have to improve on their World Cup record against European opposition if they are to stand a chance of claiming a victory here. In four meetings against teams from Europe, they have a record of one win, one draw and two losses, with the sole win coming against Serbia and Montenegro at the 2006 tournament in Germany. programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Brazil v HaitiBrazil v Haiti (Kick-off 1.30am). Mark Pougatch presents coverage of the Group C match at Philadelphia Stadium in the USA. Brazil were second best for most of their opener against Morocco, but came away with a 1-1 draw, while Haiti performed admirably in a 1-0 defeat to Scotland. Brazil have registered large victories in the two previous encounters between these nations, claiming a 6-0 win in an international friendly in 2004, and more recently a 7-1 triumph in the group stage of the 2016 Copa America, which also took place in the United States, and saw then-Liverpool attacking midfielder Philippe Coutinho score a hat-trick. Despite a relatively poor record in qualifying the Seleção will have high hopes of performing well under the stewardship of former Real Madrid, Chelsea and AC Milan manager Carlo Ancelotti, who was appointed in May last year on a one-year contract, which has since been extended for another four years, and anything other than a victory in this match will be considered a catastrophe. With analysis from Karen Carney and Emma Hayes, and commentary by Sam Matterface and Lee Dixon.

programme.title: FIFA World Cup 2026
programme.desc: Türkiye v ParaguayTürkiye v Paraguay (Kick-off 4.00am). Semra Hunter presents coverage of the Group D match at San Francisco Bay Area Stadium in Santa Clara, USA. Both sides need something from this fixture, with Türkiye abject in their 2-0 defeat to Australia, and Paraguay blown away by the USA in their opening contests. There has only been one previous meeting between these nations, a 0-0 draw in a 1995 friendly, but Paraguay will hope to emulate their results against European opposition in the group stage at their last World Cup appearance in South Africa in 2010, when they drew 1-1 against Italy and defeated Slovakia 2-0 on their way to finishing top of Group F. They subsequently overcame Japan in the last-16 via a penalty shootout, but then fell foul of a European nation in the quarter-finals, when they lost 1-0 to eventual champions Spain. With analysis from Juan Mata and Jobi McAnuff.

programme.desc: The veteran naturalist examines the world of flight, travelling across the globe to chart the evolutionary story of those creatures who seemingly defy the rules of gravity by taking to the air. Initially focusing on insects, Attenborough meets a descendant of the dragonfly, before examining the Atlas beetle, which tends to restrict flight to times when it needs a mate or a fresh supply of food. More aesthetically pleasing is a group of beautiful tropical butterflies, followed by an in-depth study into the blow fly - the jet fighter of insects

programme.title: David Attenborough's Conquest of the Skies

programme.title: David Attenborough's Conquest of the Skies

He then moves on to the floating forests of Ecuador to find out what makes the humble hummingbird tick, before ending his journey at the Gomantong bat caves of Borneo - a place he first filmed in 1972 - witnessing a mass exodus of the creatures

programme.desc: A four-part journey through Africa to experience the seasons that shape the continent. Spring in southern Africa brings long days and high temperatures, as the natural world flurries into life, transforming the continent on land and in the cold waters of the rugged coastlines. Before long, animals and plants make an an effort to reproduce and raise their young before summer dries out the lakes and rivers and takes its uncompromising hold on the planes

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: The broadcaster explores the Galapagos, a collection of volcanic islands in the Pacific known for its extraordinary wildlife. More than 150 years after Charles Darwin formulated his ground-breaking theory of evolution on the remote archipelago, Attenborough explains how life on the islands has continued to evolve in biological isolation, examining how the ever-changing volcanic landscape has given birth to species and sub-species that exist nowhere else in the world. He begins by revealing how Galapagos rose from the ocean four million years ago

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: The broadcaster reveals how life has learnt to adapt quickly in the ever-changing volcanic landscape, resulting in species that exist nowhere else in the world. David investigates the driving forces behind their evolution, exploring the appearance and behaviour of remarkable creatures and vegetation including giant whale sharks, marine iguanas and seemingly normal dandelion seeds that grow into plants the size of trees

programme.title: David Attenborough's Galapagos
programme.desc: The broadcaster concludes his exploration of the archipelago with a look at how, despite their proximity, no two of the 19 islands are the same. He also uncovers evidence that evolution on Galapagos is occurring faster than Charles Darwin could ever have imagined, and encounters Lonesome George, the last remaining giant Pinta Island tortoise, who died just a few weeks after filming in June 2012

programme.title: Jeevan Ek Sanghursh
programme.desc: Karan, a thief, works for Dr. Devraj to help keep the evil don Rattan from taking over the city. His life changes when he finds his family that had disowned him when he was a child.

programme.title: Conversation With Javed Akhtar 1
programme.desc: Lyricist, poet, screenwriter, Javed Akhtar along with film expert Nasreen Ali and Shabana Azmi, provides a fascinating and personal insight into his extraordinary life and new book Talking Life. (1/5)

programme.title: Aaghaaz
programme.desc: An honest and diligent man's life turns upside down after making an enemy in a ruthless mafia gang after he saves a girl from being molested by them.

programme.title: Barsaat Ki Ek Raat
programme.desc: Inspector Abhijeet Rai leads a harmonious life with his pregnant wife Rajni. His life comes crashing down when Kaliram, a man he had arrested five years ago, returns in his life to take revenge.

programme.title: Raksha Bandhan
programme.desc: Madhav and Pravati saved Naagrani from the clutches of snake charmer and Naagrani blessed them with a baby girl.

programme.title: Aashiqui
programme.desc: An aspiring singer meets a beautiful woman unexpectedly in a police station. He chases after her and eventually they start dating each other, but they have to deal with many problems thereafter.

programme.title: Raampur Ka Lakshman
programme.desc: While on a journey, Kedarnath Bhargav, his wife Laxmi and sons Ram and Lakshman are separated. While Lakshman stays with his father, Laxmi works as a maidservant and Ram is abducted by a criminal.

programme.title: Yaarana
programme.desc: Kishan and Bishan Kumar were childhood best friends. Young Bishan lives a wealthy life with his mom and Kishan was a former servant cum cook who later turns out to be a successful singer.

programme.title: Corporate
programme.desc: Two corporate giants compete in order to recklessly maximize their respective profits.

programme.title: Style
programme.desc: Best friends Bantu and Chantu try make two wealthy girls fall in love with them. However, they find out that the girls have been murdered and become prime suspects.

programme.title: Darna Zaroori Hai
programme.desc: Six children get lost in a forest in the middle of the night. They reach a haunted house where an old woman challenges them to sit through a narration of six horrific stories.

programme.title: Pyar Mein Twist
programme.desc: With their respective children's' marriages about to take place, two middle-aged single parents fall in love.

programme.title: Amanush
programme.desc: A village youth falsely implicated in a conspiracy is imprisoned and can't prove his innocence to his beloved. Devastated, he takes to alcohol.

programme.title: Anand Ashram
programme.desc: While the Thakur would like to get Deepak to marry a woman from an equally wealthy family, he has fallen in love with a poor woman named Asha, and would like to marry her.

programme.title: Seeta Aur Geeta
programme.desc: Identical twins Seeta and Geeta are separated at birth. One is tortured by her abusive aunt while the other grows up as a street performer. However, their lives change forever when they swap places.

programme.title: Samundar
programme.desc: An evil man Raiszada frames an innocent man for the murder of a police man, years pass by Raiszada takes full care of the police man's son, and fills his heart and mind with rage for the innocent man.

programme.title: Ilzaam
programme.desc: After Aarti's father disapproves of Ajay as his future son-in-law, he suddenly disappears from her life. Years later they meet again, but Aarti is shocked to find the truth behind his disappearance.

programme.title: Be-shaque
programme.desc: Prakash comes to a village in a bid to find his friend Shyam, who has gone missing. He is further baffled on seeing a picture of his girlfriend with a man and a child and decides to investigate.

programme.title: Disco Dancer
programme.desc: Anil's mother is falsely accused of theft and jailed. Anil swears to set this right one day. Years later, he becomes a big star and restores his mother's honour. Now his fame earns him more enemies.

programme.title: My Wife's Murder

programme.title: Tohfa
programme.desc: Two sisters fall for the same man. One of them sacrifices her love but she is carrying a secret.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E2An adrenaline-fuelled dash through nazi-occupied Europe known as ‘The Flight of the Crow’, a death-defying escape across the world’s most perilous mountain range, and the largest escape of world war two - by men who chose death over dishonour.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E3The German mass breakout that stunned wartime Britain, the astonishing secret behind the daring escape of an American bomber crew trapped in the Soviet Union, and the Trojan Horse of Stalag Luft Three.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E4The Russian soldier who led a desperate outbreak from a secret Nazi death camp, Operation Chicken - an audacious plan to flee an escape-proof Japanese prison camp, and the pilots whose bold bid for freedom won the admiration of their enemies.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E5The elite German submariners who caused havoc in the heart of the American desert, the playboy pilot they couldn’t cage, and the young lovers whose escape defied all odds.

programme.title: Greatest Escapes of WWII
programme.desc: E6Hitler’s last soldier in America who defied the FBI for 40 years, the Auschwitz prisoners who releaved the secrets of the death camps, and the merciless Nazi who almost got away.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E4A pseudoscientific theory embraced by the Nazis claimed that their Aryan ancestors had sought refuge in the Himalayas during a mythical cataclysmic ice age.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E1Nazi Germany boasted that its locomotives were faster and more innovative. This programme examines that claim by looking at these ‘flying trains’.

programme.title: Combat Trains
programme.desc: E2Veterans and historians of the Thai-Burma railway tell the story of its construction. Built to supply Japan’s invasion of India, it cost thousands of lives – both POWs and Asian slave labourers.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E1The Avro Lancaster is the legendary British heavy bomber that carved its place in history with Bomber Command during World War 2. That conflict saw over seven thousand of these iconic aircraft come off the production line.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E2Unusually, we look at the later, clipped wing version flown by Czech refugee pilots in the UK during WW2. We get close-up with a beautifully restored example, fly her and unearth long unseen test and operational footage.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E3As the Third Reich rises to power, Himmler and the SS become fixated on the Holy Grail, interpreting much of the myth surrounding it as fact - and the quest for it as attainable.

programme.title: Secret Nazi Expeditions
programme.desc: E4A pseudoscientific theory embraced by the Nazis claimed that their Aryan ancestors had sought refuge in the Himalayas during a mythical cataclysmic ice age.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E1In the wake of the First World War, Adolf Hitler identifies Benito Mussolini as his model and has one ultimate goal: to gain power in Germany.

programme.title: The Abyss: Rise And Fall Of The Nazis
programme.desc: E2Hitler appears to be eliminated after his failed putsch in 1923. Discover how the Nazi movement used democracy's tolerance in Germany to achieve a comeback with agitation and violence.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E5The aircraft capable of delivering the payload of a B17, in a single post war air frame. The many variants of this single piston engined fighter bomber helped dominate the air to ground attack role in Vietnam, earning quite a reputation.

programme.title: History's Greatest Aircraft
programme.desc: E6The definitive combat helicopter saw first blood in South East Asia and has been transport, gunship, smoke ship, command centre, MediVac and dozens of other roles. We hear and see it's hair raising missions and watch it earn its fame.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E3A chronological telling of the dramatic D-Day story, focusing on vessels that made the landings possible. From the X-Craft lying on the seabed days before the invasion to battleships like USS Texas and HMS Belfast that bombarded the Normandy beaches.

programme.title: Combat Ships
programme.desc: E4We pinpoint the moment the USA became a global superpower when we recreate how the USS Olympia won the Battle of Manila Bay, and we show how the revolutionary British HMS Dreadnought brought ship design into the 20th century.

programme.title: Ayassh Dil
programme.desc: A small-time journalist hits the big time but quickly learns that fame comes with its own set of challenges. Can they handle the pressure, or will it all crash down?

programme.title: Jabariya Jodi
programme.desc: Abhay, a righteous thug, forcefully kidnaps grooms who demand dowry and later marries them off. Babli, his childhood sweetheart, re-enters his life and changes his priorities.

programme.title: Saaransh
programme.desc: When a grieving woman discovers her new tenant is pregnant, she believes it is an opportunity for her deceased son to be reborn. Drama, starring Rohini Hattangady and Anupam Kher

programme.title: Woh Bhi Din The
programme.desc: Rohit, a photojournalist, returns to his school as a speaker. He relives his carefree days and the moment he first fell in love, filled with nostalgia.

programme.title: Hum Saath-Saath Hain
programme.desc: A woman resents her handicapped stepson inheriting her husband's estate, so gets rid of him - but her own sons do not approve. Indian Hindi-language musical drama.

programme.title: Baazigar
